arxiv-1909-00449.title: Thermal state entanglement entropy on a quantum graph
arxiv-1909-00449.creator: Alberto D. Verga, Ricardo Gabriel Elías
arxiv-1909-00449.description: Abstract A particle jumps between the nodes of a graph interacting with local spins. We show that the entanglement entropy of the particle with the spin network is related to the length of the minimum cycle basis. The structure of the thermal state is reminiscent to the string-net of spin liquids.

arxiv-2103-03025.title: Comparing multi-field primordial feature models with the Planck data
arxiv-2103-03025.creator: Dhiraj Kumar Hazra
arxiv-2103-03025.description: Abstract In this paper, we use a complete model of classical primordial standard clocks as an example to develop a methodology of directly comparing numerical predictions from complicated multi-field feature models with the Planck data, including the Planck 2018 Plik unbinned likelihood and the statistically most powerful CamSpec 2020 likelihood for temperature and polarization data.

arxiv-2104-09796.description: Abstract In this paper, we show that for sufficiently strong atomic interactions, there exist analytical solutions of current-carrying nonlinear Bloch states at the Brillouin zone edge to the model of spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) with symmetric spin interaction loaded into optical lattices.

arxiv-2307-04372.title: New results on the dynamics of critical collapse
arxiv-2307-04372.creator: Jun-Qi Guo, Yu Hu, Pan-Pan Wang 2, Cheng-Gang Shao 2
arxiv-2307-04372.description: Abstract We study the dynamics of the critical collapse of a spherically symmetric scalar field. Approximate analytic expressions for the metric functions and matter field in the large-radius region are obtained. In the central region, owing to the boundary conditions, the equation of motion for the scalar field is reduced to the flat-spacetime form.

arxiv-2309-03072.title: Character Queries: A Transformer-based Approach to On-Line Handwritten Character Segmentation
arxiv-2309-03072.creator: Michael Jungo, Beat Wolf, Andrii Maksai, Claudiu Musat, Andreas Fischer
arxiv-2309-03072.description: Abstract On-line handwritten character segmentation is often associated with handwriting recognition and even though recognition models include mechanisms to locate relevant positions during the recognition process, it is typically insufficient to produce a precise segmentation. Decoupling the segmentation from the recognition unlocks the potential to further utilize the result of the recognition.

arxiv-2310-13251.title: Stochastic Conjugate Frameworks for Nonconvex and Nonsmooth Optimization
arxiv-2310-13251.creator: Jiangshan Wang, Zheng Peng
arxiv-2310-13251.description: Abstract We introduce two new stochastic conjugate frameworks for a class of nonconvex and possibly also nonsmooth optimization problems. These frameworks are built upon Stochastic Recursive Gradient Algorithm (SARAH) and we thus refer to them as Acc-Prox-CG-SARAH and Acc-Prox-CG-SARAH-RS, respectively. They are efficiently accelerated, easy to implement, tune free and can be smoothly extended and modified.

arxiv-2402-08442.creator: Ning Chang (常宁), Zelong Yuan (袁泽龙), Yunpeng Wang (王云朋), Jianchun Wang (王建春)
arxiv-2402-08442.description: Abstract The discrete direct deconvolution model (D3M) is developed for the large-eddy simulation (LES) of turbulence. The D3M is a discrete approximation of previous direct deconvolution model studied by Chang et al. ["The effect of sub-filter scale dynamics in large eddy simulation of turbulence," Phys. Fluids 34, 095104 (2022)].

arxiv-2412-05882.title: Towards Modeling Data Quality and Machine Learning Model Performance
arxiv-2412-05882.creator: Usman Anjum, Chris Trentman, Elrod Caden, Justin Zhan
arxiv-2412-05882.description: Abstract Understanding the effect of uncertainty and noise in data on machine learning models (MLM) is crucial in developing trust and measuring performance. In this paper, a new model is proposed to quantify uncertainties and noise in data on MLMs.

arxiv-2412-08409.title: A nonreciprocal and tunable active acoustic scatterer
arxiv-2412-08409.creator: Anis Maddi, Gaelle Poignand, Vassos Achilleos, Vincent Pagneux, Guillaume Penelet
arxiv-2412-08409.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anis Maddi, Gaelle Poignand, Vassos Achilleos, Vincent Pagneux, Guillaume Penelet. This paper is part of a special issue on Active and Tunable Acoustic Metamaterials. A passive loudspeaker mounted in a duct acts as a reciprocal scatterer for plane waves impinging on either of its sides. However, the reciprocity can be broken by means of an asymmetric electroacoustic feedback which supplies to the loudspeaker a signal picked-up from a microphone facing only one of its sides.

arxiv-2501-01623.description: Abstract This paper develops instrumental variables (IV) estimators for dynamic causal effects in randomized trials with imperfect compliance. These methods are applied to a randomized trial that assigned patients with ischemic heart disease to either an invasive treatment arm centered on revascularization or a control group meant to receive non-invasive medical therapy.

arxiv-2501-15356.title: Federated Class-Incremental Learning: A Hybrid Approach Using Latent Exemplars and Data-Free Techniques to Address Local and Global Forgetting
arxiv-2501-15356.creator: Milad Khademi Nori, Il-Min Kim, Guanghui Wang
arxiv-2501-15356.description: Abstract Federated Class-Incremental Learning (FCIL) refers to a scenario where a dynamically changing number of clients collaboratively learn an ever-increasing number of incoming tasks. FCIL is known to suffer from local forgetting due to class imbalance at each client and global forgetting due to class imbalance across clients.

To accurately assess gene expression in reed canary grass under different abiotic stresses, suitable reference genes need to be identified and validated.

pmc-10737894.title: SELF-COMPASSION, DAILY STRESS APPRAISALS, AND ODDS OF ELDER ABUSE AND NEGLECT IN DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVING
pmc-10737894.creator: Carolyn Pickering, Mustafa Yildiz, Maria Yefimova
pmc-10737894.description: Stress related to behavioral symptoms is often found to be a risk factor for elder abuse and neglect in dementia family caregiving. The stress-process model suggests that stressful events alone do not determine caregiving outcomes, rather, they are impacted by personal factors which influence the response to stress.

pmc-11394838.title: Sodium Tungstate Promotes Neurite Outgrowth and Confers Neuroprotection in Neuro2a and SH-SY5Y Cells
pmc-11394838.creator: Nora Montero-Martin, María D Girón, José D Vílchez, Rafael Salto, Anna-Leena Sirén, Aleksey Zaitsev
pmc-11394838.description: Sodium tungstate (Na2WO4) normalizes glucose metabolism in the liver and muscle, activating the Mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (MAPK/ERK) pathway. Because this pathway controls neuronal survival and differentiation, we investigated the effects of Na2WO4 in mouse Neuro2a and human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma monolayer cell cultures.

pmc-11430327.title: Gastric Cancer: An Up-to-Date Review with New Insights into Early-Onset Gastric Cancer

pmc-11430327.description: Simple SummaryGastric cancer (GC) is ranked fifth among the most frequently diagnosed cancers and the fifth most common cause of cancer death in the world. We can classify cases of GC depending on the age at which it is diagnosed into early-onset GC (EOGC—up to the age of 45) and conventional GC (patients older than 45).

Electroencephalography was performed at baseline and those with active epileptiform discharges were excluded.

pmc-11637733.title: Enhancing Surgical Outcomes: Evaluating the Impact of Implementing the World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist—A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11637733.creator: ElMuhtadi B. Y. Gasoma, Mohamed A. Marouf
pmc-11637733.description: Background Globally, surgical care plays a vital role in health care. Unfortunately, complications arise in approximately 5 to 18% of surgical procedures. However, research has shown that following the surgical safety checklist provided by the World Health Organization (WHO) can significantly reduce these complications and surgery-related fatalities.

pmc-11688951.title: DEVELOPING A SUMMER RESEARCH INSTITUTE FOR EARLY CAREER RESEARCHERS
pmc-11688951.creator: Chelsea Kline, Sheryl Zimmerman, Julie Bynum, Matthew Baumgart, Sam Fazio
pmc-11688951.description: Today, there are nearly 7 million Americans living with Alzheimer’s disease and more than 11 million unpaid caregivers. These statistics highlight the need for early career investigators to join the dementia research workforce and accelerate breakthroughs in the field.
